bull_bear.body:
- Leading market position as a community industrial gas provider - pioneer of India's community boiler system (first introduced in 2014) and, per F&S, the market leader in supply of steam through community boilers
- High barriers to entry - exclusive pipeline network already laid inside industrial clusters where limited space prevents a second distribution network being built
- Only company in India supplying nitrogen through a distributed pipeline network rather than cryogenic tanks or onsite generation (Source: F&S Report)
- Sticky, contracted customer base - customer supply arrangements of 12 months to 10 years, relationships in excess of three years with all top 10 steam customers, repeat customers at 88.01% of FY25 revenue and 96.64% in H1 FY26
- Customer base grown from 91 (FY23) to 174 (H1 FY26) with reputed clients such as Aether Industries, Anupam Rasayan India, Globe Enviro Care, Gujarat Polysol Chemicals, Orgo Chem Gujarat and Subhasri Pigments
- Eco-efficient asset base - AFBC boiler designs that cut fuel consumption and SOx/NOx emissions, waste-to-energy unit at Vapi burning plastic waste and textile chindi, hydrated lime dosing, turbine co-generation at Nandesari
- Technology-led monitoring - SCADA, flow meters, steam traps/auto valves and drone mapping of the 56,236 metre pipeline network for real-time leakage, pressure, temperature and emissions tracking
- Contractual pass-through of coal cost - pricing has a fixed component with annual escalation plus a variable component linked to coal price, so raw material price increases can be passed to customers
- Experienced promoter-led management with 29 years of textile and 10 years of community boiler experience, supported by executive directors and a CFO from banking and financial services
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geographic and proximity lock-in — Every boiler and the nitrogen unit sit in Gujarat and gas can only be supplied to customers close enough to be pipeline-connected, so each facility's addressable market is a single industrial estate; growth depends on finding suitable land next to clusters and on securing and retaining pipeline rights-of-way from regulators, and there is limited physical space left for new pipelines in established estates.
- Customer concentration and contract churn — Top 10 customers were 53.95% of FY25 revenue and 52.83% in H1 FY26 with the largest alone at 23.65% in H1 FY26; contracts run 12 months to 10 years but there were instances of termination by the Company or the customer in FY25, and customers without written agreements buy on an invoice basis with no continuing obligation.
- Related party dependence on the Promoter's Sanjoo group — Transactions with Group Companies were 70.41% of FY25 revenue from operations and 61.72% in H1 FY26; Sanjoo Dyeing is simultaneously a top-10 customer, a top-10 supplier and the owner of the Sachin boilers the Company merely operates, so a large share of reported scale depends on entities controlled by the Promoter and on the continuation of arm's-length terms.
- Coal input dependence with import and supplier concentration — Coal was 76.19% of FY25 purchases and 77.97% in H1 FY26, sourced largely from Indian importers who buy Indonesian coal, with no long-term supply contracts and no FX hedging; top 10 suppliers were 91.52% of H1 FY26 purchases, so quantity or quality failure directly stops steam production even though price rises are contractually passed through.
- Leverage and capital intensity — Total borrowings were Rs 2,165.97 million as at September 30, 2025 (net debt/equity 1.42x) against net worth of Rs 1,396.70 million, with capex of Rs 1,055.36 million in FY25 alone and eight further projects planned; finance costs were 5.61% of FY25 revenue, and Rs 1,500.00 million of Fresh Issue proceeds are earmarked to repay debt, after which further expansion still requires debt or equity.
- Promoter share pledge tied to the Ascertis Credit debt — 148,874,167 Equity Shares (65.88% of paid-up capital) held by the Promoter were pledged as at the UDRHP-I date; the trustee has confirmed release before UDRHP-II filing but the shares must be repledged if the Ascertis Credit (formerly BPEA) debt is not repaid within an agreed timeline.
- Environmental and licensing exposure — The Company has previously operated a boiler before receiving final regulatory approval and received a GPCB show cause notice dated May 15, 2025 for haphazard plastic waste storage, exhaust leakages and a non-operational screw conveyor; boiler licences for the Vapi WTE unit expired on November 27, 2025 with renewal applications pending, and coal-fired operations remain exposed to tighter emission rules or fuel duties.
- Execution risk on the eight-project expansion — Capacity is planned to nearly double from 345 TPH to 675 TPH, yet Pirana and Tarapur did not have all approvals in place as at September 30, 2025, several projects have no customer tie-ups for the steam, funding is unappraised by any bank or independent agency, and utilisation is already only 45.58% (FY25), so delays, cost overruns or unfilled capacity would hit returns.

business.body: Steamhouse India generates steam in community boilers and distributes it, along with purchased third-party steam and separated/compressed nitrogen, through a dedicated pipeline network to industrial customers located in Gujarat's GIDC clusters. It operates seven community steam boilers (six owned, one leased) at Vapi Phase 1, Vapi WTE unit, Ankleshwar Phase 1 and 2, Sarigam, Nandesari and Panoli, plus one nitrogen facility at Ankleshwar, and distributes purchased steam at Dahej GIDC and Sachin GIDC. Customers are pharmaceutical, chemical, textile, agrochemical, tyre, dyes and pigments, polymer and paint manufacturers; the company also trades surplus coal bought in bulk for its own boilers.

outlook.body: The Company plans eight new or expanded community industrial gas facilities - Nandesari (Phase 2, 30 TPH, non-fossil fuel), Jhagadia (30 TPH, coal), Vapi (Phase 3, 30 TPH, non-fossil fuel), Dahej SEZ (30 TPH, coal), Ankleshwar (Phase 3, 60 TPH, coal), Pirana/Ahmedabad (30 TPH, non-fossil fuel), Panoli (Phase 2, 60 TPH, coal) and Tarapur (60 TPH, coal). Once completed, steam distribution capacity rises from 345 TPH to 675 TPH, i.e. annual installed capacity from 2,185,920.00 TPA to 4,276,800.00 TPA (assuming 330 operational days and 80% boiler efficiency). Three of these projects are funded from the Fresh Issue: brownfield expansion of Ankleshwar (120 TPH to 180 TPH, cost Rs 350.99 million, targeted August 2027), brownfield expansion of Panoli (60 TPH to 120 TPH, cost Rs 357.99 million, targeted August 2027) and a greenfield 30 TPH plant at Dahej SEZ on 30-year licensed land (total cost Rs 427.07 million of which Rs 53.27 million already spent from internal accruals, targeted October 2027). Nandesari (Phase 2), Jhagadia and Vapi (Phase 3) are targeted to start operations in calendar year 2026 and Pirana and Tarapur in calendar year 2027, funded by debt/lease finance, internal accruals and, for Pirana, a Rs 347.50 million subsidy; Pirana and Tarapur did not have all relevant approvals in place as at September 30, 2025. Alongside owned capacity, the Company intends to keep adding purchase-and-distribution arrangements (Kilburn Chemicals at Dahej, Sanjoo Dyeing at Sachin) that expand distributed volume without building a boiler, and to widen the gas slate beyond steam and nitrogen to hydrogen, instrument air and carbon dioxide.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Coal is the primary fuel and the dominant cost - cost of goods sold was 78.94% of total expenses in FY25 and 80.54% in H1 FY26; coal purchases were 76.19% of total purchases in FY25 and 77.97% in H1 FY26
- Steam pricing is split into a fixed per-unit component with built-in annual escalation for inflation and a variable per-unit component linked to the coal price, so raw material price increases are contractually passed through to customers, though cash outflows can still rise
- Indirect FX exposure - coal is bought mostly from Indian importers who source from Indonesia, with no hedging; rupee weakness against the US dollar can raise input cost
- Customer concentration - top 10 customers were 53.95% of FY25 revenue and 52.83% in H1 FY26; largest customer 16.60% in FY25 and 23.65% in H1 FY26
- Supplier concentration - top 10 suppliers were 75.35% of purchases in FY25 and 91.52% in H1 FY26
- Capital intensity and cost of funding - capex of Rs 1,055.36 million in FY25 and Rs 493.67 million in H1 FY26; finance costs were 5.61% of revenue in FY25 (6.40% FY24, 2.96% FY23) and 4.63% in H1 FY26; borrowings priced at fixed rates of 8.14%-16.08% (banks/NCDs) and 6.72%-14.25% (NBFCs)
- Revenue mix shift - purchase and distribution of steam rose to 19.71% of FY25 revenue (0.00% in FY24) and coal trading to 19.30% (0.01% in FY24), while own generation and distribution of steam fell from 99.19% of FY24 revenue to 60.56% in FY25; reported EBITDA margin moved 23.45% (FY24) to 17.54% (FY25) to 14.08% (H1 FY26)
- Related party dependence - transactions with Group Companies equalled 70.41% of FY25 revenue from operations and 61.72% in H1 FY26 (98.88%-99.46% of all related party transactions)
- Geographic concentration - all generation assets and raw material suppliers are in Gujarat, and most planned expansion is also in Gujarat
- Capacity utilisation of industrial gases sold was 45.58% in FY25 (42.88% FY24, 57.00% FY23) and 42.63% in H1 FY26, so incremental volume can be served before new capacity is required
- Competition from renewable and alternative steam sources (biomass, nuclear, green hydrogen) and from potential new entrants in industrial gases

Top 10 customers were 53.95% of FY25 revenue and 52.83% in H1 FY26 with the largest alone at 23.65% in H1 FY26; contracts run 12 months to 10 years but there were instances of termination by the Company or the customer in FY25, and customers without written agreements buy on an invoice basis with no continuing obligation.

Transactions with Group Companies were 70.41% of FY25 revenue from operations and 61.72% in H1 FY26; Sanjoo Dyeing is simultaneously a top-10 customer, a top-10 supplier and the owner of the Sachin boilers the Company merely operates, so a large share of reported scale depends on entities controlled by the Promoter and on the continuation of arm's-length terms.
risks.risk: Related party dependence on the Promoter's Sanjoo group

risks.note: Coal was 76.19% of FY25 purchases and 77.97% in H1 FY26, sourced largely from Indian importers who buy Indonesian coal, with no long-term supply contracts and no FX hedging; top 10 suppliers were 91.52% of H1 FY26 purchases, so quantity or quality failure directly stops steam production even though price rises are contractually passed through.
risks.risk: Coal input dependence with import and supplier concentration

risks.note: Total borrowings were Rs 2,165.97 million as at September 30, 2025 (net debt/equity 1.42x) against net worth of Rs 1,396.70 million, with capex of Rs 1,055.36 million in FY25 alone and eight further projects planned; finance costs were 5.61% of FY25 revenue, and Rs 1,500.00 million of Fresh Issue proceeds are earmarked to repay debt, after which further expansion still requires debt or equity.

148,874,167 Equity Shares (65.88% of paid-up capital) held by the Promoter were pledged as at the UDRHP-I date; the trustee has confirmed release before UDRHP-II filing but the shares must be repledged if the Ascertis Credit (formerly BPEA) debt is not repaid within an agreed timeline.
risks.risk: Promoter share pledge tied to the Ascertis Credit debt

risks.note: The Company has previously operated a boiler before receiving final regulatory approval and received a GPCB show cause notice dated May 15, 2025 for haphazard plastic waste storage, exhaust leakages and a non-operational screw conveyor; boiler licences for the Vapi WTE unit expired on November 27, 2025 with renewal applications pending, and coal-fired operations remain exposed to tighter emission rules or fuel duties.

Capacity is planned to nearly double from 345 TPH to 675 TPH, yet Pirana and Tarapur did not have all approvals in place as at September 30, 2025, several projects have no customer tie-ups for the steam, funding is unappraised by any bank or independent agency, and utilisation is already only 45.58% (FY25), so delays, cost overruns or unfilled capacity would hit returns.
risks.risk: Execution risk on the eight-project expansion

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Backward: coal is the primary fuel and is bought in bulk, primarily imported Indonesian coal, through three routes - from Indian importers after the coal has cleared Indian customs, on a 'high seas basis' (purchased while in transit at sea, with the Company then responsible for customs clearance), and directly from overseas suppliers on a CIF basis with the Company clearing customs. Coal price is based on or linked to the fluctuating international price of coal. This bulk coal position is monetised in two directions: it fuels the boilers, and the excess is sold in the open market as a coal-trading line that was 28.14% of revenue from operations in H1FY26 and 19.30% in Fiscal 2025 (an invoice-only / purchase-order business with no fixed coal supply contracts). Purchase geography (state-wise bifurcation of raw materials): Gujarat 1,643.57 million / 99.99% in H1FY26, 2,728.56 million / 96.23% in Fiscal 2025, 1,700.86 million / 78.19% in Fiscal 2024 and 2,064.71 million / 88.64% in Fiscal 2023, with the balance from Dadra & Nagar Haveli, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and outside India. Fuel is being progressively diversified away from coal into non-fossil sources - plastic waste, textile chindi, agro-waste, refuse-derived fuel, waste gas and textile waste - with the 15 TPH Vapi WTE unit already commissioned on non-fossil fuel and Nandesari (Phase 2), Vapi (Phase 3) and Pirana (Ahmedabad) planned on non-fossil fuel; at Pirana the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation supplies the waste-dumping-site land, half the capex and a 347.50 million subsidy under a 10-year work order. Distribution pipe is sourced domestically. Utilities: power is drawn from the local state power grid plus captive electricity from back-pressure turbines at Nandesari, with turbines planned at other locations. Quality control begins at procurement with high-GCV coal in the 3,217-5,204 KCal range; hydrated lime is sprinkled on coal to cut SOx, and fly ash is disposed of per state pollution-control requirements. Forward: the Company owns, operates and maintains the entire distribution layer - a 56,236 meter operational pipeline system as of November 15, 2025 (55,916 m at September 30, 2025, up from 27,085 m at March 31, 2023), running on pipeline rights-of-way easements and connecting into customer-owned pipes at the customer's premises, with individual pipelines spanning 3,000 to 20,000 meters. Real-time monitoring uses flow meters, SCADA, steam traps/auto valves, third-party sensor and data-visualisation providers over a custom API and SQL database, and drone mapping for leak detection; emissions parameters (SPM, SOx, NOx and, for waste-fired boilers, HCl) are tracked. Customers control their own offtake via site valves without disturbing the generating system. A deliberately capital-light forward variant is the 'purchase and distribution' model, in which the Company buys unused or by-product steam from third-party industrial units and distributes it through its own pipelines - already in place with Kilburn Chemicals Limited, at Dahej GIDC, and at Sachin GIDC with Group Company Sanjoo Dyeing and Printing Mills Private Limited, which owns the generation assets while the Company operates and maintains those boilers and distributes the steam. This line went from effectively nil in Fiscal 2024 (0.02 million) to 778.91 million / 19.71% in Fiscal 2025 and 411.11 million / 17.24% in H1FY26. Related-party density runs through both ends of the chain: Sanjoo Dyeing & Printing Mills Private Limited was simultaneously the largest customer (563.88 million / 23.65% of revenue in H1FY26) and the fourth-largest supplier (142.74 million / 8.68% of purchases in H1FY26). Workforce as of September 30, 2025: 213 employees (142 in facility operations, 17 accounts and finance, 16 admin and HR, 8 aviation, 8 management, 7 legal and compliance, 5 each in IT & automation, sales and marketing, and procurement) plus 292 contract labourers (136 Ankleshwar, 50 Nandesari, 34 Sarigam, 38 Vapi, 34 Panoli); attrition 10.12% in H1FY26, 37.83% in Fiscal 2025, 22.74% in Fiscal 2024 and 30.29% in Fiscal 2023. Inventories were 309.16 million at September 30, 2025 (461.02 million at March 31, 2025, 462.27 million at March 31, 2024, 83.18 million at March 31, 2023) with inventory turnover of 5.81 (not annualised), 6.16, 3.89 and 27.33 respectively.

market_position.basis: Community industrial-gas generation and centralised distribution (steam and nitrogen) through a dedicated pipeline network, serving industrial clusters in Gujarat. The DRHP's qualitative factors claim a 'Leading market position offering customers an energy efficient solution' and 'High barriers to entry for competitors' (Source: F&S Report). The Company and its Promoters are described as pioneers of the community boiler system in India, first introduced in 2014, with first-mover advantage; the F&S report states Steamhouse is the only company in India that supplies nitrogen using a distributed pipeline network instead of cryogenic tanks/onsite generation, and that its Ankleshwar nitrogen plant is India's first and only common nitrogen facility. Seven community steam boilers (Vapi Phase 1, Vapi WTE, Ankleshwar Phase 1, Ankleshwar Phase 2, Sarigam, Nandesari, Panoli) with combined installed steam capacity of 345 TPH (2,185,920.00 TPA) and 56,236 metres of operational pipeline as of November 15, 2025. The DRHP discloses no market-share percentage for the Company.

orders_not_placed.note: The DRHP states verbatim, separately for each of the three capex objects: 'We are yet to place any order for plant and machinery. Further, the quotations received from vendors in relation to the proposed expansion are valid as on the date of this Updated Draft Red Herring Prospectus-I. We have not entered into any definitive agreements with any of the vendors...'. Every one of the component tables (boiler and boiler parts, plant and machinery, steel structure, electrical, instrument, labour, pipeline) carries the matching disclaimer that quotations have been received from several third-party vendors but no definitive agreements have been entered into with any of them. Accordingly every machinery line recorded above is a quotation only, not a placed order, and order_placed is false throughout. No percentage of capex is stated in the document and the DRHP's own capex totals for the three projects are the only stated aggregates, so pct_of_capex is left null rather than derived. A dedicated risk factor is cross-referenced on page 72: 'The Objects of the Offer include orders for equipment and machinery which have not yet been placed. Further, we are yet to place orders for capital expenditures. overview.business_model: The Company runs three industrial-gas offerings plus a trading line. (1) Generation and distribution of steam: it owns and operates seven community steam boilers in Gujarat (Vapi Phase 1, Vapi WTE unit, Ankleshwar Phase 1, Ankleshwar Phase 2, Sarigam, Nandesari, Panoli), burning mainly coal, and pipes the steam to industrial customers who would otherwise each run a captive boiler - this was 53.97% of revenue from operations in the six months ended September 30, 2025 and 60.56% in Fiscal 2025. (2) Purchase and distribution of steam: it buys steam produced by other steam-generating entities in Dahej GIDC and Sachin GIDC and distributes it through its pipelines - 17.24% of H1 FY2026 revenue and 19.71% of Fiscal 2025 revenue. (3) Separation, compression and distribution of nitrogen: it extracts nitrogen from atmospheric air at its Ankleshwar facility (capacity 350 NM3/hour, commercial operations from February 1, 2025) and supplies it by pipeline - a small 0.13% of H1 FY2026 revenue (Rs 3.01 million) and 0.02% of Fiscal 2025 (Rs 0.90 million). (4) Because it procures coal as primary fuel, it also trades coal on an invoice-only basis - 28.14% of H1 FY2026 revenue and 19.30% of Fiscal 2025 revenue, including supplies to group companies Sanjoo Dyeing & Printing Mills Private Limited and Sanjoo Prints Private Limited as related-party transactions. As of November 15, 2025 combined installed steam capacity across the seven boilers was 345 TPH (2,185,920.00 TPA assuming 330 operational days and 80% boiler efficiency) served by 56,236 metres of operational pipeline. Revenue from operations was Rs 2,384.17 million for the six months ended September 30, 2025, Rs 3,951.06 million in Fiscal 2025, Rs 2,917.10 million in Fiscal 2024 and Rs 3,155.39 million in Fiscal 2023. It served 174 customers in H1 FY2026, 173 in Fiscal 2025, 125 in Fiscal 2024 and 91 in Fiscal 2023; repeat customers were 96.64% and 88.01% of revenue in H1 FY2026 and Fiscal 2025 respectively, and the top 10 customers were 52.83% and 53.95%.

genesis.founding_story: The Company and its Promoters are described (per the Frost & Sullivan 'Industry Report on Community Industrial Gases Generation & Distribution in India' dated November 28, 2025) as pioneers of the community boiler system in India, which was first introduced in 2014 - a model in which one central boiler and a dedicated pipeline network replace captive boilers at each individual industrial customer. Incorporated in 2015 as Ankleshwar Eco Energy Limited by Vishal Sanwarprasad Budhia (the sole individual Promoter interested in the promotion or formation of the Company), it built its first facility at Vapi GIDC in 2017 and expanded cluster by cluster across Gujarat, renaming itself Steamhouse India Limited in 2021. Having established the steam business, it is now extending the same pipeline model to other industrial gases, commencing nitrogen production and supply on February 1, 2025 - stated to be the only company in India supplying nitrogen through a distributed pipeline network rather than cryogenic tanks or onsite generation (Source: F&S Report).

strategy_growth.title: Competition from industrial gas generation companies, customers' own boilers and future entrants

concerns_observed: The revenue base runs through Promoter-controlled Group Companies. Related party transactions with Group Companies were Rs 1,471.62 million (H1 FY26), Rs 2,781.79 million (Fiscal 2025), Rs 1,036.66 million (Fiscal 2024) and Rs 518.56 million (Fiscal 2023), being 61.72%, 70.41%, 35.54% and 16.43% of revenue from operations; total related party transactions were 62.42%, 70.79%, 37.74% and 17.98%. Sanjoo Dyeing & Printing Mills Private Limited is simultaneously the largest customer (Rs 563.88 million / 23.65% of revenue in H1 FY26; Rs 656.03 million / 16.60% in Fiscal 2025) and a top-ten supplier in all four periods (Rs 142.74 million / 8.68% of purchases in H1 FY26; Rs 329.08 million / 11.61% in Fiscal 2025).

Two thirds of the paid-up capital is pledged against a single lender's debt. 148,874,167 Equity Shares, 65.88% of paid-up Equity Share capital, are pledged by Promoter Vishal Sanwarprasad Budhia. Catalyst Trusteeship Limited confirmed by letter dated June 27, 2025 that the pledge will be released prior to filing of the UDRHP-II, 'and the same will be required to be repledged if our Company is unable to repay the entire debt of Ascertis Credit (Formerly known as BPEA) within an agreed timeline'. The Ascertis non-convertible debenture, sanctioned Rs 1,700.00 million on August 25, 2023 at a stated IRR of 16.08%, had Rs 300.33 million outstanding at September 30, 2025 and carries a 3% prepayment penalty on IPO proceeds.

Fiscal 2025 growth did not come from the core offering. Generation and distribution of steam — the owned-boiler business — fell to Rs 2,392.86 million (60.56% of revenue) in Fiscal 2025 from Rs 2,893.66 million (99.19%) in Fiscal 2024, while coal trading rose to Rs 762.45 million (19.30%) from Rs 0.19 million (0.01%) and purchased steam rose to Rs 778.91 million (19.71%) from Rs 0.02 million. The MD&A states 'The majority of these [coal] sales were to Sanjoo Dyeing' and that the shift followed termination of the Company's lease of the Sachin GIDC steam generation facilities from Sanjoo Dyeing, after which 'Sanjoo Dyeing resumed manufacturing of steam at these facilities; and we resumed supplying coal'.

Profit before tax fell in the growth year and profit after tax rose only on a lower tax rate. The MD&A states profit before tax 'decreased by 10.02% to Rs 389.65 million for Fiscal 2025 from Rs 433.04 million for Fiscal 2024', while profit after tax rose 14.62% to Rs 311.61 million from Rs 271.86 million; total tax expense of Rs 78.05 million was 20.03% of profit before tax in Fiscal 2025 against Rs 161.18 million or 37.22% in Fiscal 2024. Fiscal 2025 profit after tax of Rs 311.61 million remains below Fiscal 2023's Rs 333.99 million on a larger revenue base.

Every printed margin and return metric is on a declining path. EBITDA margin 18.36% (Fiscal 2023), 23.45% (Fiscal 2024), 17.54% (Fiscal 2025), 14.08% (H1 FY26); PAT margin 10.55%, 9.27%, 7.82%, 5.46%; Return on Equity 58.76%, 26.26%, 23.53%, 8.92% (not annualised); Return on Capital Employed 32.88%, 20.24%, 17.20%, 7.66% (not annualised). On the DRHP's own H1 FY26 peer columns, EBITDA margin was 14.08% against 39.44% for Linde India Limited and 37.14% for Ellenbarrie Industrial Gases Limited, and PAT margin 5.46% against 22.74% and 28.83%.

Utilisation is low and uneven while the plan is to roughly double capacity. Capacity utilisation for industrial gases sold was 57.00% (Fiscal 2023), 42.88% (Fiscal 2024), 45.58% (Fiscal 2025) and 42.63% (H1 FY26). Facility level in H1 FY26 / Fiscal 2025: Sarigam 13.77% / 13.22%, Panoli 3.61% / not operational, Vapi Phase 1 30.49% / 40.70%, Nandesari 50.46% / 35.24%, Ankleshwar Phase 1+2 55.84% / 55.38%. Eight further facilities are under construction, taking installed capacity from 345 TPH (2,185,920.00 TPA) to 675 TPH (4,276,800.00 TPA). The DRHP states costs other than fuel have limited correlation with production.

Working capital has gone negative and is financed by stretching suppliers. Net Working Capital was Rs (579.19) million / (44) days at September 30, 2025, Rs (189.56) million / (18) days at March 31, 2025, Rs 259 million / 32 days at March 31, 2024 and Rs (96) million / (11) days at March 31, 2023. Trade payables rose to Rs 1,072.01 million / 82 days from Rs 780.36 million / 72 days, Rs 364.16 million / 46 days and Rs 217.15 million / 25 days over the same dates, across 235 creditors of which 64 are MSMEs owed Rs 28.57 million.

Closing cash and cash equivalents are negative in every period presented, stated net of bank overdraft: Rs (151.81) million (Fiscal 2023), Rs (163.51) million (Fiscal 2024), Rs (199.00) million (Fiscal 2025) and Rs (36.11) million at September 30, 2025. Cash from investing was Rs (896.28) million, Rs (1,259.08) million, Rs (1,229.94) million and Rs (623.11) million across the same periods, financed by financing inflows of Rs 367.67 million, Rs 1,037.23 million, Rs 123.47 million and Rs 60.29 million.

Credit ratings were cut and none has been assigned since. By ICRA letter dated October 30, 2024 every rated facility was downgraded one notch — long term fund based term loan Rs 81.80 crores to ICRA BBB (Stable) from BBB+ (Stable), long term/short term unallocated Rs 53.18 crores to BBB (Stable)/A3+ from BBB+ (Stable)/A2, short term non fund based letter of credit Rs 42.00 crores to A3+ from A2 — and the DRHP states 'The Company has not had any ratings assigned till date during the current fiscal.'

The capital expenditure objects rest entirely on quotations. All 163 machinery line items across Ankleshwar (Phase 3), Panoli (Phase 2) and Dahej SEZ carry order_placed false, and the DRHP repeats for each object 'We are yet to place any order for plant and machinery... We have not entered into any definitive agreements with any of the vendors'. Risk Factor 44 quantifies the exposure: 'Our Company proposes to utilize an amount of Rs 1,082.78 million for funding capital expenditure towards purchase of equipment and machinery... no orders for purchase of the equipment and machinery are yet to be placed.' Most quotations are dated October 1-10, 2025 and valid 8 months or 240 days, with the Thermax Babcock & Wilcox boiler quotations dated October 27, 2025 valid to April 30, 2026, while deployment runs into Fiscal 2028 with commissioning of Ankleshwar (Phase 3) and Panoli (Phase 2) in August 2027 and Dahej SEZ in October 2027.

Past projects have overrun on both schedule and cost, and eight more are in flight. Nandesari Phase 1: scheduled March 2023, actual September 2023; sanctioned cost Rs 150.00 million against actual Rs 358.90 million. Panoli: scheduled October 2023 and March 2023, actual June 2025; sanctioned Rs 230.00 million against actual Rs 343.70 million. Nandesari Phase 2 was scheduled for September 30, 2025 and is now intended for Calendar Year 2026. Capital commitments not provided for stood at Rs 916.00 million as at September 30, 2025, separate from the Net Proceeds objects.

Ownership is near-total and the entry price is near zero. Promoters hold 221,160,725 Equity Shares (97.87%) and the Promoter Group a further 1,852,350 (0.82%); the Company has 94 Shareholders in all per the beneficiary position statement dated December 5, 2025. Average cost of acquisition is Rs 0.04 per Equity Share for Vishal Sanwarprasad Budhia (202,500,000 shares) and Nil for Ritu Budhia and the three Promoter trusts, against the March 28, 2024 private placement at Rs 200 per Equity Share and secondary transfers at Rs 220 in October and November 2024. Two bonus issues built the stake — 4:1 on November 1, 2022 (60,000,000 shares) and 2:1 on October 5, 2023 (150,000,000 shares) — after the face value was sub-divided from Rs 10 to Rs 2 on September 30, 2022.

Rs 800.00 million of the Rs 4,250.00 million Offer is a secondary sale by the same Promoter whose shares are pledged: 'The Promoter Selling Shareholder shall be entitled to the net proceeds from the Offer for Sale... and our Company will not receive any proceeds from the Offer for Sale.'

Input dependence is concentrated on one commodity and a short supplier list with no long-term contracts. Coal purchases were Rs 1,281.72 million / 77.97% of total purchases (H1 FY26), Rs 2,160.50 million / 76.19% (Fiscal 2025), Rs 2,001.50 million / 92.01% (Fiscal 2024) and Rs 2,234.11 million / 95.91% (Fiscal 2023). Top ten suppliers were 91.52%, 75.35%, 76.53% and 79.43% of purchases over the same periods, the largest being Maheshwari Logistics Limited at Rs 357.93 million / 21.78% in H1 FY26. The Company states it does not hedge and has indirect USD exposure through Indian importers.

Six categories of past non-compliance are disclosed. Statutory-dues delays fell from 15 instances / Rs 0.16 million (Fiscal 2023) to 6 / Rs 0.19 million, 7 / Rs 0.14 million and 1 / Rs 0.04 million; the Sachin premises of Group Company Sanjoo Dyeing were occupied without GIDC subletting permission between Fiscal 2022 and Fiscal 2024, voluntarily disclosed by letter dated July 23, 2024, with GIDC imposing a penalty on Sanjoo Dyeing; the Panoli boiler commenced operation on June 5, 2025 on a provisional approval dated June 3, 2025 with final CCA only on June 23, 2025; MIDC assessed an additional premium of Rs 14.78 million at Tarapur for failure to construct in time; two Gujarat Stamp Act orders dated October 15, 2025 assess Rs 8.25 million and Rs 27.52 million; and CARO clause (iii) comments report demand loans without stipulated repayment schedules in Fiscal 2025 and Fiscal 2023.

The Company states it 'has also received closure notice from state pollution control board for some of our units', without naming the units, the dates or the outcome, alongside the disclosed record of operating a boiler before final approval.

The Promoter Group is incomplete by the Company's own admission. Ambika Agarwal, a relative of the Promoter, refused to provide required information, confirmations and undertakings including details of her Connected Entities; SEBI, by letter dated October 6, 2025 (SEBI/HO/CFD/RAC-DIL2/P/OW/2025/25967/1), did not accede to the exemption sought under Regulation 300(1)(c) and directed reliance on publicly available information, so complete disclosures on her and her Connected Entities cannot be assured.

The Company is entering an unrelated business from a related party. It obtained a DGCA Non-Scheduled Operator licence on October 21, 2025 valid to October 20, 2030 and leased a six-seater single-engine aircraft from Sanjoo Dyeing Inc., a US subsidiary of a Group Company, at an annualised rental of US$240,000 per annum, bearing all operating expenses including fuel, maintenance, crew, insurance, parking and landing charges; rent expense to Sanjoo Dyeing INC was Rs 38.7 lakhs (Fiscal 2025) and Rs 25.8 lakhs (H1 FY26). The DRHP states the Company, its Promoters and management have no experience managing aircraft operations, and 8 of the 213 employees at September 30, 2025 sit in an 'Aviation' department.

Attrition among permanent employees was 30.29% (Fiscal 2023), 22.74% (Fiscal 2024), 37.83% (Fiscal 2025) and 10.12% (H1 FY26), and 'as on the date of this Updated Draft Red Herring Prospectus – I, we do not have key man insurance policies.'

Customer relationships are concentrated and partly uncontracted. Top ten customers were Rs 1,259.55 million / 52.83% (H1 FY26), Rs 2,131.67 million / 53.95% (Fiscal 2025), Rs 1,744.12 million / 59.79% (Fiscal 2024) and Rs 2,011.83 million / 63.76% (Fiscal 2023). Agreements with the top ten run two to seven years — one expiring in Fiscal 2026, four in Fiscal 2027 and one in Fiscal 2029 — and four of the top ten have no agreement at all and purchase on a purchase-order basis. There were 14 instances of customer agreement termination across H1 FY26 and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023.

Two Promoter Group entities are in the same line of business. Sanjoo Dyeing & Printing Mills Private Limited and Sanjoo Prints Private Limited generate and supply steam, and Promoter Vishal Sanwarprasad Budhia and Executive Director Yadav Lalankumar Dayanand are directors of both. Sanjoo Dyeing's own industrial gas revenue was Rs 142.73 million / 5.99% of its total revenue from operations in H1 FY26 and Rs 328.48 million / 8.31% in Fiscal 2025. Non-compete and exclusivity agreements dated April 1, 2025 are in place, but the DRHP gives no assurance these companies will not compete in future, and the Sachin facilities run under an O&M agreement with Sanjoo Dyeing expiring three years from April 1, 2025.

Unsecured borrowings jumped fivefold in six months to Rs 333.51 million at September 30, 2025 from Rs 66.75 million at March 31, 2025 — body corporate Rs 233.35 million, purchase financing Rs 37.05 million and credit card balance payable to bank Rs 63.11 million — availed from banks and from the Promoter and Promoter Group members and stated to be recallable.

Revenue is single-state and single-segment: '100% of our revenue from the sale of industrial gases was earned from customers in Gujarat' in all four periods, all operating facilities are in Gujarat, and the business constitutes one reportable segment. The only facility outside Gujarat, Tarapur, is unbuilt and under a construction deadline of January 6, 2026.

The nitrogen line is a single-customer business: 'we currently only have one customer for our nitrogen business.' It generated Rs 0.90 million (0.02% of revenue) in Fiscal 2025 and Rs 3.01 million (0.13%) in H1 FY26, and no capacity utilisation table is printed for it.

An emphasis of matter attaches to the interim numbers: the December 1, 2025 report on the Special Purpose Consolidated Interim Ind AS Financial Statements draws attention to the purpose and basis of preparation and to 'non-inclusion of comparative amounts for the six months period ended September 30, 2024 and accounting ratio for the six months period ended September 30, 2024', so H1 FY26 has no prior-half comparative in the document. The opinion is stated not to be modified.

Contingent liabilities were Rs 108.25 million as at September 30, 2025 (Order of Superintendent of Stamps Rs 35.77 million, Bank Guarantee Rs 72.47 million, income tax litigation Rs 0.01 million), against Rs 76.62 million, Rs 44.36 million and Rs 43.00 million at the three preceding year ends.
data_gaps: PLACEHOLDER IN THE DRHP — this is a UDRHP-I, so there is no Price Band and no Offer Price. The number of Equity Shares in the Fresh Issue and the Offer for Sale, post-Offer paid-up capital, post-Offer promoter and public shareholding percentages, the general corporate purposes amount, the Net Proceeds and the Total row of the objects table, the issuer's own P/E and market capitalisation, the Minimum Promoters' Contribution table and every lock-in expiry date are printed as [bullet]. No valuation, dilution or per-share Offer arithmetic can be derived from this document and none is attempted here.

NOT DISCLOSED — no order book, orders-in-hand or unexecuted-order value appears anywhere in the DRHP; the terms 'order book', 'orders in hand' and 'unexecuted' do not occur. Forward revenue is described only qualitatively (contracts of 12 months to 10 years, minimum consumption clauses, 3% to 10% fixed-cost escalation) and volume tie-ups for facilities under construction are stated in TPH/TPD, not value.
NOT DISCLOSED — the DRHP states no market-share percentage for the Company, in either the issuer chapters or the Frost & Sullivan report; positioning is recorded as qualitative only.

NOT DISCLOSED — no top-5 customer or supplier cut exists in the document; only largest, top 3 and top 10 are printed, so those fields are null rather than estimated. Three of the H1 FY26 top-ten suppliers are unnamed — 'Supplier 4' Rs 178.93 million / 10.89%, 'Supplier 5' Rs 156.15 million / 9.50%, 'Supplier 9' Rs 43.05 million / 2.62%.
NOT DISCLOSED — no B2B/B2C numeric split is printed; the DRHP states only that the business 'is predominantly conducted on a business-to-business basis'.

NOT DISCLOSED — no quality-management or product certifications (ISO or equivalent) appear in the document; the 'awards, accreditations or recognitions' table carries awards and honours only. The empty certifications list reflects the document, not an extraction failure.

NOT DISCLOSED — financial information for the five Group Companies (Sanjoo Dyeing and Printing Mills, Sanjoo Prints, Sanjoo Filaments, Brickcrest Infrasol, Sanjoo Dyeing INC) is not set out in the DRHP; it is stated to be hosted on the Company's website and no website link is stated for Sanjoo Dyeing INC. Their revenue and profit therefore cannot be assessed against the related-party flows that make up 70.41% of Fiscal 2025 revenue.

NOT COMPARABLE — the Statutory Auditors' report dated December 1, 2025 carries an emphasis of matter on the 'non-inclusion of comparative amounts for the six months period ended September 30, 2024 and accounting ratio for the six months period ended September 30, 2024', so no H1-on-H1 comparison exists in the document. H1 FY26 return ratios are marked 'not annualised' by the issuer and are not annualised here.

NOT DISCLOSED — no cash conversion cycle is printed; the DRHP gives debtor days (22 / 29 / 28 / 32), inventory days (10 / 58 / 43 / 24) and creditor days (25 / 46 / 72 / 82) separately, and no combined figure is derived here.

NOT DISCLOSED — the nitrogen facility has no per-fiscal installed-capacity or utilisation table; only the 350 NM3/hour nameplate and the revenue lines (Rs 0.90 million Fiscal 2025, Rs 3.01 million H1 FY26) are printed. The company-level capacity KPI expressly excludes nitrogen.

ADMITTED INCOMPLETE BY THE ISSUER — following SEBI's letter dated October 6, 2025 refusing the Regulation 300(1)(c) exemption, the Company states it cannot assure that complete disclosures relating to Promoter Group member Ambika Agarwal and her Connected Entities are included; what is disclosed rests on public searches of MCA, CIBIL, Watchout Investors, the Fugitive Economic Offenders list, NCLT, SEBI and the Income Tax Tribunal websites.

UNQUANTIFIED IN THE DRHP — the disclosed closure notice from a state pollution control board names no unit, no date, no breach and no outcome; and the percentage of capex represented by unplaced machinery orders is not stated by the document, so only its own Rs 1,082.78 million figure is quoted and no percentage is computed.

INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY IN THE DRHP — the nitrogen plant's stated CCA sequence (application May 12, 2025, provisional approval June 20, 2023, final CCA June 23, 2025) cannot be read in that order; and the Government and Other Approvals section states no material approvals have expired and are yet to be renewed while Risk Factor 10 discloses the Vapi WTE boiler licences expired on November 27, 2025 with renewal awaited.

ATTRIBUTION — the pioneer-of-the-community-boiler claim, the 'high barriers to entry' claim, the 'only company in India' nitrogen-pipeline claim and all industry sizing derive from the Frost & Sullivan 'Industry Report on Community Industrial Gases Generation & Distribution in India' dated November 28, 2025, commissioned under an engagement letter dated December 21, 2024 and paid for by the Company for this Offer; the DRHP notes investors may not be able to seek legal recourse for losses from reliance on it.

DIRECTIONAL SEPARATION — litigation by the Company (1 criminal matter, Rs 0.90 million) and litigation against the Company (Rs 52.68 million across 3 tax, 3 statutory or regulatory and 1 material civil matter) are opposite-direction exposures and are quoted separately throughout; the rolled-up store's code-computed combined figure is not used and no sum of the two is stated here.

UNITS — the DRHP prints every rupee figure in Rs millions; the extraction store holds the same figures in Rs lakhs (a factor of ten). All amounts in this verdict are quoted as the document prints them, in Rs millions, except where an object amount is given in both.

open_questions: On what timeline must the Ascertis Credit debt (sanctioned Rs 1,700.00 million on August 25, 2023 at a stated 16.08% IRR, Rs 300.33 million outstanding at September 30, 2025) be repaid for the 148,874,167 pledged shares to stay released, and what happens to the 65.88% pledge if that timeline is missed after listing?

Would the business have grown at all in Fiscal 2025 without the Group Company flows, given generation and distribution of steam fell to Rs 2,392.86 million from Rs 2,893.66 million while coal sales of Rs 762.45 million went mostly to Sanjoo Dyeing and purchased steam of Rs 778.91 million came through Dahej and Sachin?
Why did the effective tax rate fall from 37.22% (Fiscal 2024) to 20.03% (Fiscal 2025), and is the Rs 13.75 million deferred tax charge against Rs 62.19 million in the prior year repeatable?

What are the pricing and margin terms of the Sachin O&M arrangement and the April 1, 2024 steam purchase and supply agreement with Sanjoo Dyeing, and what happens to 61.72% of revenue if the O&M agreement is not extended beyond its three-year term from April 1, 2025?

Why was the Company's lease of the Sachin steam generation facilities from Sanjoo Dyeing terminated in Fiscal 2025, moving the asset ownership and the steam-generation margin back to the Group Company while the Company took on coal supply to it?
Which units received the closure notice from the state pollution control board, on what date, for what breach, and what was the outcome?

How is the Rs 916.00 million of capital commitments and the balance capital expenditure on the eight facilities under construction (Nandesari Phase 2, Jhagadia, Vapi Phase 3, Pirana, Tarapur and others) to be funded, given none of them is a Net Proceeds object and Net Working Capital is Rs (579.19) million?

What happens to the Ankleshwar (Phase 3), Panoli (Phase 2) and Dahej SEZ cost estimates when the October 2025 quotations (8 months / 240 days validity; Thermax to April 30, 2026) expire before the Fiscal 2027 and Fiscal 2028 deployment tranches?

Will 40% of construction at Tarapur be completed by January 6, 2026 as required by the MIDC order dated August 12, 2025, and what further premiums arise if not, given only Rs 85.82 million of the Rs 450.00 million project cost had been spent by September 30, 2025?

What is the commercial rationale for the Company bearing an aircraft lease of US$240,000 per annum from a Group Company's US subsidiary plus all operating costs, and what revenue, if any, is the DGCA Non-Scheduled Operator permit expected to generate?
Why has no credit rating been assigned during the current fiscal following the October 30, 2024 ICRA downgrade, and has the Company sought one?
What drove permanent-employee attrition to 37.83% in Fiscal 2025 from 22.74% in Fiscal 2024, and why is there still no key-man insurance?

Will the Vapi WTE boiler licences that expired on November 27, 2025 be renewed, and how does that reconcile with the Government and Other Approvals statement that no material approvals have expired and are yet to be renewed?
What information about Ambika Agarwal and her Connected Entities is missing from the disclosure following SEBI's October 6, 2025 refusal of the exemption, and could any of it be material?
When is a second customer expected for the nitrogen facility, which has run since February 1, 2025 on a 350 NM3/hour nameplate with revenue of Rs 3.01 million in H1 FY26 and no published utilisation?

What are the outcomes sought in the appeals against the two Gujarat Stamp Act orders dated October 15, 2025 (Rs 8.25 million and Rs 27.52 million, 25% deposited, payable within 90 days with 12% per annum interest thereafter)?

parameter_scores.basis: Every positioning claim — pioneer of the community boiler system introduced in 2014, 'high barriers to entry', the only company in India distributing nitrogen by pipeline, and India's first common nitrogen facility — derives from the Frost & Sullivan 'Industry Report on Community Industrial Gases Generation & Distribution in India' dated November 28, 2025, commissioned under an engagement letter dated December 21, 2024 and paid for by the Company for this Offer. The DRHP discloses no market-share percentage for the Company anywhere. Two listed peers are named (Linde India Limited, Ellenbarrie Industrial Gases Limited) plus two unlisted competitors (PR Ecoenergy Private Limited, Detox India Private Limited) shown as 'NA' for Fiscal 2025.

red_flags: Transactions with Promoter-controlled Group Companies equalled 70.41% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2025 and 61.72% in H1 FY26, up from 16.43% in Fiscal 2023, with the same counterparty acting as largest customer and top-ten supplier simultaneously; the Group Companies' own financial statements are not printed in the DRHP but hosted on the Company's website.

148,874,167 Equity Shares — 65.88% of paid-up Equity Share capital — are pledged by the Promoter against Ascertis Credit debt, and the DRHP states the shares 'will be required to be repledged if our Company is unable to repay the entire debt of Ascertis Credit... within an agreed timeline'.

Profit before tax fell 10.02% to Rs 389.65 million in Fiscal 2025 while profit after tax rose 14.62% to Rs 311.61 million, the difference being an effective tax rate that dropped from 37.22% to 20.03%.

The Fiscal 2025 revenue increase came mainly from a coal-trading line described as 'invoice only' that went from Rs 0.19 million to Rs 762.45 million, majority-directed to Group Company Sanjoo Dyeing, while the owned-boiler steam line fell from Rs 2,893.66 million to Rs 2,392.86 million.

Closing cash and cash equivalents are negative in every period presented net of bank overdraft — Rs (151.81), (163.51), (199.00) and (36.11) million — alongside Net Working Capital of Rs (579.19) million and creditor days rising from 25 to 82.
ICRA downgraded every rated facility one notch on October 30, 2024 and 'The Company has not had any ratings assigned till date during the current fiscal.'

Rs 1,082.78 million of equipment and machinery to be funded from the Net Proceeds is backed by quotations only; all 163 machinery lines carry no placed order and no definitive vendor agreement, and the quotations are stated to be valid 8 months or 240 days from dates of October 1-10, 2025 (Thermax boiler quotations to April 30, 2026) against deployment scheduled into Fiscal 2028.

SEBI refused, by letter dated October 6, 2025, the exemption sought for Promoter Group member Ambika Agarwal, who declined to provide required confirmations, so the Promoter Group disclosure is admittedly incomplete.

Two Gujarat Stamp Act orders dated October 15, 2025 assess Rs 8.25 million and Rs 27.52 million of duty and penalty on a 2022 amalgamation and on GIDC lease deeds, payable within 90 days with 12% per annum interest thereafter, with only 25% deposited.

The Company discloses it 'has also received closure notice from state pollution control board for some of our units', without naming the units, dates or outcome, alongside operating the Panoli boiler on a provisional approval from June 5, 2025 before the final CCA of June 23, 2025.

The Vapi WTE boiler licences expired on November 27, 2025 with renewal awaited, while the Government and Other Approvals section of the same document states that no material approvals have expired and are yet to be renewed.

The Company leased an aircraft from Sanjoo Dyeing Inc., a US subsidiary of a Group Company, at US$240,000 per annum plus all operating expenses, entering a business in which it states its Promoters and management have no experience.
Permanent-employee attrition was 37.83% in Fiscal 2025 and 30.29% in Fiscal 2023, with no key-man insurance policies as at the date of the UDRHP-I.

Registered-office and steam-sourcing arrangements at Sachin ran between Fiscal 2022 and Fiscal 2024 without the requisite GIDC subletting permission, voluntarily disclosed only on July 23, 2024, with GIDC penalising the Group Company that owns the plot.
strengths_observed: Physical network in place and growing: seven operational community steam boilers (six owned, one leased) with combined installed capacity of 345 TPH (2,185,920.00 TPA) and 56,236 metres of operational pipeline as of November 15, 2025, against cumulative boiler capacity of 285 TPH (Fiscal 2025), 270 TPH (Fiscal 2024) and 240 TPH (Fiscal 2023) and cumulative pipeline of 47,526 m, 41,539 m and 27,085 m at the same dates, per the Chartered Engineer certificate of Dr. P. J. Gandhi dated December 1, 2025.

Reported top line grew in Fiscal 2025 after a decline: revenue from operations Rs 3,951.06 million (Fiscal 2025), Rs 2,917.10 million (Fiscal 2024), Rs 3,155.39 million (Fiscal 2023) and Rs 2,384.17 million for the six months ended September 30, 2025; the DRHP's own KPI table prints revenue growth of 35.44% in Fiscal 2025 against (7.55)% in Fiscal 2024.

Return ratios as printed sit above both listed peers: Return on Equity 23.53% and Return on Capital Employed 17.20% for Fiscal 2025, against ROE of 11.91% for Linde India Limited and 16.88% for Ellenbarrie Industrial Gases Limited in the Basis for Offer Price comparison table.

Customer base widened and repeats are high: 174 customers in the six months ended September 30, 2025, 173 (Fiscal 2025), 125 (Fiscal 2024) and 91 (Fiscal 2023); repeat customers were 151, 120, 74 and 68 and contributed 96.64%, 88.01%, 91.49% and 90.29% of revenue from operations. Four of the top ten customers in H1 FY26 have a relationship spanning over five years.

Contract architecture passes the main input cost through: customer supply agreements run 12 months to 10 years, prices carry a variable component that 'moves in line with the coal prices' plus a fixed component with 'a reserve escalation year on year that ranges between 3% to 10%', and many contracts carry a minimum consumption level with deficit-consumption charges recoverable.

No borrowing default is disclosed in any period presented: 'We have not had any default under any of our borrowings during the six months period ended September 30, 2025 or during Fiscal 2025, Fiscal 2024 or Fiscal 2023', against total borrowings of Rs 2,165.97 million as at September 30, 2025 (Rs 1,832.46 million secured).

The largest single object reduces leverage: Rs 1,500.00 million (15,000.00 lakhs) of Net Proceeds is earmarked for repayment or prepayment of borrowings against total outstanding borrowings of Rs 2,165.97 million as at September 30, 2025, itemised lender by lender with sanction date, sanctioned amount, tenor, rate and prepayment penalty, and scheduled entirely in Fiscal 2026.

A capital-light second line scaled quickly: purchase and distribution of third-party steam went from Rs 0.02 million (Fiscal 2024) to Rs 778.91 million / 19.71% of revenue from operations (Fiscal 2025) and Rs 411.11 million / 17.24% (H1 FY26), operated at Dahej GIDC and Sachin GIDC without owning the generating assets.

Waste-fired and municipal-tie-up capacity is live rather than only planned: the 15 TPH Vapi WTE unit commenced February 1, 2025 on plastic waste, textile waste, agro-waste and RDF and ran at 68.05% utilisation in H1 FY26 against 40.12% in its two operating months of Fiscal 2025; the Pirana (Ahmedabad) project carries a 10-year work order from the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation with land, half the capital expenditure and a Rs 347.50 million subsidy stated to carry no repayment obligation.

Litigation is small and affirmatively Nil outside the Company: by the Company 1 criminal proceeding aggregating Rs 0.90 million; against the Company 3 tax proceedings, 3 statutory or regulatory actions and 1 material civil litigation aggregating Rs 52.68 million, with criminal Nil. By and against the Directors (other than Promoters), the Promoters, the KMP and Senior Management, and the Subsidiary, every category is disclosed as Nil.

Cost estimates for the three capex objects are third-party certified: the project report dated December 1, 2025 of Dr. P. J. Gandhi, Chartered Engineer supports the Ankleshwar (Phase 3) Rs 350.99 million, Panoli (Phase 2) Rs 357.99 million and Dahej SEZ Rs 427.07 million estimates, and Statutory Auditors Natvarlal Vepari & Co certified by certificate dated December 8, 2025 the Rs 53.27 million already incurred on the Dahej SEZ land lease advance from internal accruals.

Board and committee structure is in place ahead of listing: 6 Directors of whom 3 are Independent, including one woman Independent Director, with Audit, Nomination and Remuneration, Stakeholders' Relationship, Risk Management and CSR Committees constituted between April 2022 and February 2023 and the Audit Committee chaired by an Independent Director.
